# Leslie Moore

## Overview

- **Age:** 28 years old  <sub>[v4 c10 P49](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0049), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015)</sub>
- **Role:** Keeps summer boarders and former school teacher at Glen school  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022), [v4 c26 P3](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0003)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mrs. Moore  <sub>[v4 c8 P17](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0017)</sub>; Mrs. Dick Moore  <sub>[v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Leslie is a tall, slender woman who inherited her mother's great beauty, spirit, and striking figure. She has milk-white skin, sea-blue or shining gray-green eyes, and brown, work-hardened hands. Her long, splendid golden hair gleams like molten gold in the light and falls to her feet. She often wears a touch of crimson, such as a scarf or a flower at her throat, to complement her appearance.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P17](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0017), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c12 P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 c12 P21](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0021), [v4 c16 P11](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0011), [v4 c21 P17](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0017), [v4 c23 P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024), [v4 c26 P18](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0018), [v4 c33 P16](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0016), [v4 c38 P1](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0001)_

## Personality

Leslie possesses a glowing, pent-up, and intensely emotional personality that can be reserved, cold, and bitter under the weight of past sorrow. She has a resolute nature and a deep, unswerving sense of duty passed down by her grandmother. Although she can take sullen spells when burdened, in congenial company she is animated, witty, clever, and friendly. She is fiercely ambitious, possesses brilliant brains, and displays a deep love and clannish devotion to her loved ones.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P17](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0017), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022), [v4 c12 P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 c17 P10](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0010), [v4 c21 P13](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0013), [v4 c23 P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024), [v4 c25 P15](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0015), [v4 c30 P27](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0027), [v4 c31 P0](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0000)_

## History

Leslie West grew up as the daughter of Frank and Rose West, surviving the traumatic childhood loss of her brother Kenneth and later finding her father after his suicide. She studied at Queen's Academy using an inheritance from her grandmother and became a schoolteacher at the Glen school. At sixteen, she was coerced into marrying Dick Moore to save her mother's farm from foreclosure, and she lost her mother to pneumonia a year later. After her husband was believed to have returned mentally incapacitated from a sea voyage, she faithfully nursed him for years in poverty. Following Gilbert Blythe's suggestion, she agreed to take him to Montreal for an operation, where it was discovered that the man was actually Dick's lookalike cousin, George Moore, freeing her from her long burden. She later fell in love with Owen Ford, accepting his proposal of marriage, and made plans to marry him at Christmas.

## Background by volume

- witnessed the accidental death of her four-year-old brother Kenneth when she was twelve  <sub>[v4 c11 P16](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0016)</sub>
- found her father Frank West after he committed suicide when she was fourteen  <sub>[v4 c11 P4](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0004), [v4 c11 P20](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0020)</sub>
- attended Queen's Academy on an inheritance from her Grandmother West and taught at the Glen school  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022)</sub>
- coerced into marrying Dick Moore at age sixteen to prevent foreclosure on her mother's farm  <sub>[v4 c10 P49](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0049), [v4 c11 P26](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0026)</sub>
- lost her mother to pneumonia a year after her marriage  <sub>[v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028)</sub>

## Quotes

> I am Leslie Moore—Mrs. Dick Moore  <sub>[v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>

> I was sixteen. I am twenty-eight now. Well, I must go back.  <sub>[v4 c10 P49](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0049)</sub>

> I ENVY Anne, and I’d envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I’d gladly give my life for THAT!  <sub>[v4 c19 P28](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0028)</sub>

> There is no cage. But—it doesn’t seem as if there were anything else, Anne. You—you remember what I told you of my folly that night on the sand-bar? I find one doesn’t get over being a fool very quickly. Sometimes I think there are people who are fools forever. And to be a fool—of that kind—is almost as bad as being a—a dog on a chain.  <sub>[v4 c33 P14](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0014)</sub>

> Anyhow, I have YOU. Life can’t be altogether empty with such a friend. Anne, pat my head—just as if I were a little girl—MOTHER me a bit—and let me tell you while my stubborn tongue is loosed a little just what you and your comradeship have meant to me since that night I met you on the rock shore.  <sub>[v4 c33 P17](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0017)</sub>
